origin.description: Repeat the characters of each string, optionally with a separator between copies.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector, or another vector that can be coerced to character.

arguments.name: times
arguments.text: How many times to repeat each string.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: A single string inserted between copies. NULL repeats with nothing between the copies.

origin.details: string and times are recycled with vctrs. NULL is left as NULL and the result is empty. A length-zero vector cannot be recycled to a length greater than one. With sep set, paste indexes the original string, so a length-1 string and a longer times is subscript out of bounds, and a missing string is written as the letters NA. A negative times is missing when sep is NULL and an error when sep is set.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as the recycled string and times.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "pear", "banana")
cat(paste0("str_dup(fruit, 2) returns ", paste(str_dup(fruit, 2), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_dup(fruit, 1:3) returns ", paste(str_dup(fruit, 1:3), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))
cat(paste0("str_dup(c(\"a\", NA), 2, sep = \"-\") returns ", paste(str_dup(c("a", NA), 2, sep = "-"), collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Repeat each string by calling vctrs.vec_recycle_common and then stringi.stri_dup.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is R's NULL.

arguments.name: times
arguments.text: A count, or a list of counts. A fractional count is truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: None joins the copies directly. Any other single string is inserted between them.

translation.details: None does not enter the recycle. A real empty list does, and a length other than 0 or 1 raises. With sep set, the original string is indexed, and a missing element becomes the letters NA. Names on string are repeated when a length-1 vector is recycled.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing result is stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.dup import str_dup
fruit = ["apple", "pear", "banana"]
print("str_dup(fruit, 2) returns " + ", ".join(str_dup(fruit, 2)) + ".")
print("str_dup(fruit, 1:3) returns " + ", ".join(str_dup(fruit, [1, 2, 3])) + ".")
na = str_dup(["a", NA], 2, sep="-")
print("str_dup(c(\"a\", NA), 2, sep = \"-\") returns " + ", ".join("NA" if item is NA else item for item in na) + ".")
